cues.say: Pre-scaling is a practice, not a product. You add server copies and upgrade the database before a spike you know is coming, instead of waiting for the system to react.
You can do it by hand, from a checklist, or set it up as a scheduled scaling rule in your cloud.
Why not just rely on autoscaling? Autoscaling means the cloud watches a number, like CPU, and adds copies when your servers get busy.
But it's slow on purpose. It waits until servers have been busy for a few minutes, so it doesn't react to a blip. Then new copies take minutes to boot and pass health checks.
Meanwhile, the spike is already here, and customers see errors. The new copies arrive too late.
Pre-scaling flips the order. You know when the spike is coming, so you get ready an hour before.
Add server copies, say from two to six.
Upgrade the database to a bigger size. That often means a short restart, so do it early, in a quiet hour.
Warm the CDN, so your busiest pages are already cached.
And keep autoscaling on, as a safety net, in case the spike is bigger than you planned.
Use it for any spike you can see coming: a sale you scheduled, an email to every customer, a TV mention or a big game.
Now a real case. The snow forecast airs on the six PM news, and tire shop traffic jumps twenty times in two minutes.
Without pre-scaling, autoscaling notices the busy servers at six oh six, and new copies are ready at six oh nine. That's four minutes of errors, at the worst possible moment.
With pre-scaling, at five PM the shop goes from two copies to six, upgrades the database, and warms the CDN. The spike arrives at six oh five, and the system is already sized.
This applies to every busy part: more API copies, a bigger database, a warm CDN. Workers scale too, but on queue length, not CPU.
Two trade-offs. You pay for idle copies for a few hours. That's cheap next to four minutes of errors.
And it only works for spikes you can see coming. Surprises still need autoscaling, rate limits and a waiting room.
In the interview, say: autoscaling reacts in minutes. The spike arrives in seconds.
